BillHeading.Sponsors: Senate Behavioral Health Subcommittee to Health & Long Term Care (originally sponsored by Senators Zeiger, O'Ban, Dhingra, and Wagoner)
BillHeading.BriefDescription: Concerning persons with substance use disorders.

BillBody.BillTitle: AN ACT Relating to persons with substance use disorders; adding new sections to chapter 71.24 RCW; providing an effective date; and providing an expiration date.

BillSection.BillSectionHeader: Sec. 1. A new section is added to chapter 71.24 RCW to read as follows:
BillSection.P: (1) Every patient who presents to an emergency room, evaluation and treatment center, crisis triage facility, or crisis stabilization unit with an indication of a substance use disorder, opioid overdose, or chronic addiction, in the professional opinion of the medical staff, must receive, with patient consent, prior to discharge:
(a) A screening for the need for substance use disorder services using a validated screening tool;
(b) If the screening indicates a need for substance use disorder services, a referral for a substance use disorder evaluation and appropriate services;

(c) If the screening indicates a need for substance use disorder services, and the patient consents, a referral to a certified substance use disorder peer counselor, including transmittal of patient information to the certified substance use disorder peer counselor or agency providing certified substance use disorder peer counselor services so that outreach can be made to the patient; and
(d) Access to information about available substance use disorder treatment services.
(2) The facts of the screening or patient refusal and any other action taken under this section must be noted in the patient's medical record.
(3) The requirements of this section may be satisfied through the use of telemedicine or other innovative service models.

(4) The requirements of this section may not be used to extend the length of stay of a patient in an emergency room, evaluation and treatment center, crisis triage facility, or crisis stabilization unit.

BillSection.BillSectionHeader: Sec. 2. A new section is added to chapter 71.24 RCW to read as follows:
BillSection.P: (1) The authority must develop and disseminate best practice protocols for the use of facilities under section 1 of this act, including guidance for identifying clients who present with an indication of a substance use disorder, opioid overdose, or chronic addiction, and for referring them for an evaluation and appropriate services.

(2) The authority must develop a system to make accurate information about clinically appropriate substance use disorder services available to facilities under section 1 of this act and must develop a strategy to update this information.
(3) The authority and the department may independently develop rules to implement this act.

BillSection.BillSectionHeader: Sec. 3. A new section is added to chapter 71.24 RCW to read as follows:
BillSection.P: (1) The authority shall prepare a gap analysis and implementation plan for delivery to the governor and appropriate committees of the legislature by December 1, 2021, to implement sections 1 and 2 of this act, including an analysis of workforce needs and proposals to provide the needed level of services.

BillSectionHeader.P: Sections 1 and 2 of this act take effect January 1, 2024.
